image.description:
Image is AniList's medium portrait, about 100px wide; ImageLarge the
same at about 230px for cards that show it bigger than a thumbnail
(empty on cache entries written before it existed).

anilist.ListEntryDetail.description: Entry is null when the title is not on the list

scoreRaw.description:
ScoreRaw is the score on the 100-point scale, whatever format the
user rates in; 0 is unrated

anilist.Media.description: Media is the resolved provider record behind the unit, for a detail view

airingSchedule.description:
AiringSchedule is every not-yet-aired episode AniList has dated ahead
(usually the whole current cour), for the multi-week calendar view.

color.description:
Color is the artwork's dominant colour as a hex string. The poster
frame shows it while the file loads. Empty on older cache entries
and for artwork AniList has not measured.

extraLarge.description:
ExtraLarge is the same artwork at twice the edge (460px rather than
230px). A poster tile on a phone is around 200 CSS px wide, which a
230px file has to stretch two to three times over at the device
pixel ratios those screens run at. Empty on cache entries written
before the field existed; consumers fall back to Large.

medium.description:
Medium is the 100px-wide artwork, for list rows and thumbnails
where Large would be downloaded only to be shrunk. Empty on cache
entries written before the field existed; consumers fall back to
Large.

descriptions.description:
Descriptions is the overview per UI language ("de", "en") where the
provider has more than one: TVDB and TMDB translate theirs, the
cached record serves every user, and the page picks the one its
reader speaks. Description stays the instance's default.

externalLinks.description:
ExternalLinks are the streaming and official sites AniList lists for
the title; the Crunchyroll one carries the series id the dub recorder
reads releases under (see CrunchyrollID).

nextAiringEpisode.description:
NextAiring is the upcoming episode's release slot (RELEASING titles);
nil for finished titles or cache entries predating the field.

popularity.description:
Popularity is the audience size (AniList: users on their lists, TMDB:
vote count). Comparable within one source, which is all the catalog
sorts across: the metadata source is picked per folder.

schedule.description:
Schedule is the flattened release list (absolute episode numbers), filled
from AiringSchedule.Nodes here and from season episodes by TMDB. Ahead of
now, except for the week TMDB keeps behind it for the airings recorder.

schema.description: Schema is the payload version this entry was written with, see MediaSchema.

native.description: original-script title, stored per locale, never displayed directly

preferred.description:
Preferred is the canonical display title we compute (localized,
never native Japanese). Set by the API layer once the media's source
is known; consumers render this instead of guessing romaji/english.

type.description:
Type is ANIME or MANGA (light novels are MANGA with format NOVEL).
AniList ids are unique across both, so one id never means two works.

volumes.description:
Volumes and Chapters are the MANGA counterparts of Episodes, 0 while
the work is still running or AniList does not know.

isLiked.description: IsLiked: the reading user likes it; always false on an anonymous read

dub.description: the dub this slot releases, short tag (de, en); "" = the original

est.description: projected from the original plus the lag, not a date anyone published

have.description: the episode is in the local folder already

remoteAt.description:
RemoteAt: when the episode's file reached the server - the first check
that queued it - or, before it has, when it should, from the slot plus
the upload lag learned on this watch (RemoteEst). Only on the slots of
the track the watch fetches; 0 when nothing is known yet.

api.AnilistPermissions.description: Allow: the write switches, off until the user turns them on

list.description:
List: status, progress, score and removal of list entries, and the
watched-episode step from the suggestions page and the player

social.description: Social: replies and likes in forum threads

passwordReset.description: a forgotten password can be reset by mail (SMTP and base URL are set)

recursive.description: required to delete a non-empty directory

cover.description:
Cover and Section as the client sent them on hiding; empty for items
hidden before they were kept

flat.description: no subfolder: files straight into localPath

skipped.description:
why nothing was queued, when nothing was: without these a sync that had
nothing to do is indistinguishable from one that failed

cover.description: provider poster url, loaded straight by the browser

coverLarge.description:
CoverLarge is the same poster at twice the edge (AniList's extraLarge),
for a srcset; empty where the provider has only the one size

folder.description: remote show folder, the parent of a season subfolder

title.description: empty when the folder has no catalog match

dub.description:
Dub and Sub are the audio and subtitle languages the names advertise,
as app language codes ("Ger", "Jap")

res.description:
Res is the video height the file names advertise (1080 for "1080p"),
0 when they say none

secs.description:
Secs and Rate describe a done download's last run: how long it took
and its mean speed in bytes per second. Zero when not measured.

title.description: episode title, only when the provider cache is warm

ids.description: every queued download of the caller, in the new order

api.DubProgress.description:
DubProgress: a dub the older files carry and the newer ones lack, read
from the names or the releases they came from; nil when there is none.

expectedAt.description: forecast of Next's dub; 0 = no date known

lang.description: the code as the names spell it (Ger, Eng, ...)

next.description: first episode after the last dubbed one

released.description: Next's dub is out already, ExpectedAt is when

probed.description:
Probed: how the languages above were established - 0 nothing measured yet,
1 read from the container streams, 2 measuring was attempted and the
container would not answer. The card shows this so a disputed suggestion
can be judged without reading the log.

soft.description:
Soft is the subset of Sub the copy can hand over as a selectable track
(subtitle stream or sidecar file). A language in Sub but not in Soft is
burned into the picture, and the card says so.

episodes.description: dupep: the episode numbers present twice

keep.description: folder of the copy bestCopy would keep

twice.description:
Twice: dupep only, the files behind each doubled episode, so one of
them can be sent to the trash from the card.

why.description: one line, in the user's language

path.description: local folder or file from a duplicate card

api.EpRef.description: first episode after the last dubbed one

code.description: Code is host_key_unknown (first contact) or host_key_mismatch.

newKey.description:
NewKey is the offered key (base64); echo it back to /trust-hostkey on
accept so exactly the reviewed key gets pinned.

oldFingerprint.description: OldFingerprint is empty on first contact.

stopped.description: the job keys that were cancelled

paused.description: job families that will not start

subfolderSeparator.description: replaces spaces in a title folder; "" keeps them

subfolderSource.description:
SubfolderSource names the subfolder: "remote" after the remote folder,
"title" after the series title, "none" for none at all. The title is
resolved once, in the dialog that creates the sync, and lands in the
watch as part of LocalPath - see aiWatchFields.

localRoot.description: destination folders are rebased onto this

server.description: server to create (protocol/port/password confirmed by the user)

serverId.description: reuse an existing server instead of creating one

watches.description: the reviewed plan rows; empty on a dry run

id.description: old syncMap id, also the UI row key

api.LibraryRoots.description: Returns the instance settings (admin only). Secrets are reported as set/unset flags only, never their values.

folder.description: local dir, or a "plex:" key when it is not a shared mount

api.LocalStat.description:
Local: what the folder holds on disk. Only set for the local catalog,
where the question is "what do I have", not "what can I fetch".

hasPassword.description: false for an account that only signs in through OIDC

locale.description: the language mail and push go out in (de or en)

tvdbApiKeySet.description:
which metadata providers the instance has keys for, so every user (not
only an admin, who can read the settings) is offered their options

upgradeRequired.description:
what must be replaced before the app opens: "password" (the policy
refuses the current one) or "passkey" (one signed in without user
verification); empty when nothing is due

code.description:
Code names the cause: cert_untrusted, tls_unsupported, auth_failed or
connect_failed.

force.description: Force saves the switch without the connection test passing.

port.description:
Port is the FTPS port: 21 for explicit TLS (AUTH TLS), 990 for implicit
TLS. Zero keeps the stored port.

api.PlayAnilist.description: Anilist is per user, set on the answer, never on the cached info

anilist.description: Anilist is per user, set on the answer, never on the cached info

fonts.description: Fonts are the font attachments by stream index, for /api/play/font

bytes.description:
Bytes read from the remote source by the runs open on it, and their
rate in bytes per second; 0 for a local file

done.description:
Done is the share of the awaited segment written (0-1), Left the
seconds still to go at the run's Speed (1 = as fast as playback); -1
when no segment is awaited or the number is not known yet

file.description: File is a sidecar subtitle beside the video; Index is -1 then

image.description:
Image marks a picture subtitle (PGS, VobSub, DVB): it cannot be rendered
as text. PGS goes out as SUP for the browser to draw (format=sup), the
others are burned into the transcoded picture

title.example: Re:ZERO - Starting Life in Another World

source.description:
Source names the route that resolved it: manual (set by hand), series (the
ids the series carries), path (the folder Plex scanned), title (guessed),
none (unresolved - nothing is changed in the library).

base.description: Base is the URL prefix every entry is served under: Base + entry path.

pages.description: comic pages in order, relative to Base

needsApproval.description: an admin has to let the account in before it can sign in

name.description: new base name, no path separators

path.description: entry to rename, under an allowed root

serverId.description: ServerID is the server whose index holds it, 0 for the local library

level.description:
"risk": fix it before exposing the instance; "warn": should be fixed;
"info": worth knowing; "ok": checked and fine

end.description: unix second of the newest sample

samples.description: bytes per second, one sample per second, oldest first

disk.description:
Disk is the download root's filesystem, kept for consumers that read
one value; Disks is every filesystem the library spans, the root first

totalBytesPerSec.description:
TotalBytesPerSec sums the running transfers; EtaSeconds is the
queue's remaining bytes at that rate, 0 while nothing moves.

because.description: recommended: the finished titles behind it

kind.description:
Kind, for incomplete: season (missing season/movie), sequel (Plex
chain) or episodes (gaps in an owned season).

library.description: incomplete: Plex library title, for grouping

missing.description: incomplete/episodes: the episode numbers a remote copy has and the local season lacks

sync.description: incomplete (missing unit): where a one-off sync creates the season/movie folder

why.description: one line, in the user's language: why this is listed

builtAt.description:
BuiltAt is when the lists were assembled (unix seconds), so the page
can say how current they are; 0 when not known (no blob yet).

duplicates.description: the same season/movie held twice, or an episode twice in one folder

api.SyncPlan.description: incomplete (missing unit): where a one-off sync creates the season/movie folder

replace.description:
Replace: the copy this sync improves on is trashed once the new file is
in place (upgrades only; a missing episode has nothing to replace).

separator.description:
Separator replaces spaces in the rendered name; "" keeps them. Part of
the plan because it belongs to the template it was configured with.

subfolder.description: false: the template controls the folder structure

template.description: rename template (may carry a "Season NN/" or "{title}/" subfolder)

dir.description: the folder it came from, and returns to

expiresAt.description: unix seconds: when the sweep deletes it

files.description: rows behind this entry: the video and its sidecars

reason.description:
Reason is why it is here: "upgrade" (a better copy replaced it) or
"duplicate" (cleared from the duplicates view); empty for older rows

replacedBy.description: ReplacedBy is the file name of the copy an upgrade put in its place

size.description: bytes, sidecars and folder contents included

key.description: Key is the base64 host key from the failed test's newKey field.

order.description:
Order lists the enabled axes most important first. It picks the remote
copy that gets recommended, sorts the suggestions, and tells the
assistant what counts as the better copy.

soft.description:
Soft: the same language, but as a selectable track instead of burned into
the picture. Its own axis because it is its own decision - someone who
already reads the German signs may not care, and someone who wants to turn
them off cares about nothing else.

category.description: anime-movie | anime-tv | movie | tv, for grouping

improvesSoft.description:
ImprovesSoft: the remote copy offers a subtitle language as a SELECTABLE
track that the local one only shows burned into the picture.

languageUnverified.description:
LanguageUnverified: the sub/dub gain above rests on one side's file names
because its container would not answer, so it cannot be confirmed from
here - the local copy may already carry the track without a language tag.
The finding stands, the card says it is unconfirmed.

localSeasons.description: every season of this show the library already has, this one included

media.description: Media is the resolved provider record behind the unit, for a detail view

sync.description: where a one-off sync writes (into the existing local season/movie folder)

why.description: one line, in the user's language: what the better copy adds

probed.description:
Probed: how the languages above were established - 0 nothing measured yet,
1 read from the container streams, 2 measuring was attempted and the
container would not answer. The card shows this so a disputed suggestion
can be judged without reading the log.

soft.description:
Soft is the subset of Sub the copy can hand over as a selectable track
(subtitle stream or sidecar file). A language in Sub but not in Soft is
burned into the picture, and the card says so.

airedMapping.description: resolve absolute episode numbers to aired-order S/E via TVDB/TMDB (endless series)

airings.description: every scheduled future release the provider knows (multi-week calendar)

attention.description:
Attention: why this watch needs a hand, ordered by severity; empty =
fine. The one needs-attention source - dashboard, tile and the machine
status all read this, never their own arithmetic.

behind.description: episodes aired per AniList but not yet available locally (the source release can lag the original broadcast)

behindLate.description:
BehindLate: Behind holds more episodes than the last behindGrace of
releases explains - the source is not just a few hours behind.

checkAttempts.description:
CheckAttempts counts consecutive failed checks; > 0 means the watch is
on the short retry backoff and NextCheck is that retry, not the interval.

dubExpectedAt.description: forecast unix seconds of the next dub release; 0 = no date known

dubLagDays.description: days the WantDub release trails the original when no release has shown the lag yet; 0 = observed only

dubNextEpisode.description: the episode the filtered dub is waited for, local numbering

dubOverdue.description: the forecast plus a week of grace passed without a release

dubProgress.description:
DubProgress: a dub the older files carry and the newer ones lack, read
from the names or the releases they came from; nil when there is none.

dubWaiting.description:
DubWaiting: the watch is caught up on the dub it filters for; the
original is ahead but the dub is not due yet - expected waiting, not
something to look at.

fromEpisode.description: count only local episodes >= this (shared season folder); 0 = all

intervalMin.description: global setting, echoed for the UI

langWaiting.description: videos on the remote skipped by the dub/sub filter, target not yet local

langWaitingEps.description:
LangWaitingEps: which episodes the dub/sub filter held back at the
last check (LangWaiting is their count); empty when the names carry
no SxxEyy.

lastOwned.description: files skipped at the last check because the library holds the episode under another name

lastQueued.description: files queued at the last check, -1 = none yet

lastResult.description: error text of the last check, "" on success

lastUploading.description: files still uploading remotely at the last check

mediaId.description: linked AniList/TMDB id → metadata (cover, episodes, airing); 0 = auto/none

mediaSource.description: metadata provider for a manual link: "anilist" | "tmdb:tv" | "tmdb:movie"

missing.description: gaps below the newest local episode (e.g. have 1,2,3,5 → 4 is missing), independent of airing state

nextCheck.description: unix seconds of the next scheduled check, mirroring WatchLoop's due rule

nextEpisodeAbs.description: absolute AniList number, shown in parens when it differs

offset.description: {episode-N} renumber offset: absolute episode = local - offset (for showing the original number)

plexAudioLang.description: after sync, select this audio language in Plex; "" = don't touch

plexStreamMiss.description:
PlexStreamMiss: what the preference could not deliver on this watch's
files, a CSV of "audio" and "sub"; "" = everything asked for was there.

plexSubLang.description: after sync, select subtitles in Plex: "" = don't touch, "off" = none, "Ger" = full, "Ger:forced" = forced

renameSeriesId.description: explicit provider series id for rename; 0 = auto

renameTitleLang.description: BCP-47 for the localized rename title; "" = Plex/system language

replaceOld.description:
ReplaceOld is read by the one-off sync only (an upgrade): the copy an
episode improves on is moved to the trash once the new file is in place.
Not stored on a watch - a watch with a rename rule already overwrites
re-releases by name.

seasons.description: seasons the local folder holds (specials left out), ascending

seenEpisodes.description: watched episodes from the linked AniList list

subfolder.description: write into local_path/<remote name> instead of local_path directly

unsorted.description: episodes waiting in the collecting folder for the provider to list their number

wantDub.description: sync only files tagged with this dub language code (e.g. "Ger"); "" = any

wantSub.description: sync only files tagged with this sub language code; "" = any

queued.description:
with wait=1: what the check did. Queued are the new download ids, so
the caller can follow them; Error is a failed check's reason

season.description:
Season is the season the folder holds, 0 for a movie or a folder that
holds season subfolders itself. SeasonFolder is the folder that season
gets ("Season 02", spelled like a sibling when the library has one),
LibraryDir the show root the library already holds - the sync goes there
rather than to the kind's default folder.

title.description:
Title is the series title of that folder - the catalog match, or the
guess from the folder name when it is unmatched. It is what a "title"
subfolder is named after.

absolute.description: the provider's absolute number, when it has one

aired.description: YYYY-MM-DD, "" when the provider has no date

local.description: local number, only when a {episode-N} template renumbers it

season.description: the season the local files are filed under

upcoming.description: dated in the future, so its absence is not a gap

missing.description: episodes in the list the folder does not hold

replaceDue.description: signed in without verifying the user; to be replaced

path.description: the directory that refused the write

bytes.description:
Bytes is the stored payload size; cache stores only, 0 elsewhere (an
estimate for the other tables would be a guess dressed up as a number).

keptOnReset.description: KeptOnReset marks the stores a default reset walks past.

needs.description: Needs lists the stores that must be filled before this one can be.

oldest.description: Oldest/Newest are SQLite UTC stamps, "" when the store has no time column.

pruneSec.description:
PruneSec is how long the sweep keeps this store's rows before deleting
them, 0 = kept until overwritten; Prunable counts the rows past that.
A stale row is still served while its refetch runs - these are the ones
nothing will read again.

rebuild.description: Rebuild is the job/mechanism slug that refills the store, "" = on demand.

ttlSec.description: TTLSec and Stale are cache stores only (0 elsewhere).

logLevel.description: LogLevel is the current effective log level (trace|debug|info|warn|error).

title.description: from the media cache, "" when unresolved

images.description: Images are data URLs (image/*) the user attached, read by a vision model

tools.description:
Tools the user switched on for this chat beyond the built-in ones:
"web_search" (with fetch_page). Mode "research" turns the web tools on
and briefs the model for a multi-step report with many more rounds.

vision.description: Vision per model: true, false, or null when the endpoint does not say

webSearch.description: WebSearch: a SearXNG is set, so the web tools can be switched on

replaceOld.description:
ReplaceOld is set on upgrades only: the dialog offers to trash the copy
the sync improves on (see replaceOldCopy).

seasonFolder.description:
SeasonFolder travels the same way: the season folder a title subfolder
gets under it ("Season 02"), empty when the season belongs to the
template or the folder is not a season.

subfolderSource.description:
SubfolderSource and SubfolderSeparator travel to the dialog only: it
names a "title" subfolder from the title in front of the user and folds
it into LocalPath before saving, so no watch ever carries them. A reader
that ignores them still gets the right folder from Subfolder.

scoreRaw.description: ScoreRaw is the score on the 100-point scale, 0 to clear it

canEdit.description: CanEdit: the user allowed WeebSync to change the list

entry.description: Entry is null when the title is not on the list

episodes.description: Episodes the media has, 0 when unknown (still airing, say)

linked.description:
Linked: an AniList account is connected; everything else is empty
without one

scoreFormat.description:
ScoreFormat is the scale the user rates in: POINT_100,
POINT_10_DECIMAL, POINT_10, POINT_5 or POINT_3

threadId.description:
ThreadID is the thread a liked comment belongs to, so its cached pages
are dropped; the thread's own id for type THREAD

allow.description: Allow: the write switches, off until the user turns them on

parentCommentId.description: ParentCommentID answers that comment; absent answers the thread

plexFolder.description: matching Plex folder basename, if any

large.description: Large is the same picture at its original size, for screens that need more

api.bannerFocus.description:
Focus is where the banner's detail lies, for the page to pick the
slice its box shows; absent until the server has read the picture

bundle.description: other folders in the same directory with the same series: one card

pick.description: the pick replayed now; 0 when nothing reached the bar

scored.description: false for TMDB and TVDB: their search is not replayed here

sequelFrom.description: set when the SEQUEL chain moved the pick to the season the folder names

source.description:
the source the folder is matched on (catalogue and auto-sync alike),
which a correction searches

kind.description:
Kind: heuristic movie/series classification, so films mixed into a series
library are told apart. "" when nothing is conclusive.

local.description:
Local: what the folder holds on disk. Only set for the local catalog,
where the question is "what do I have", not "what can I fetch".

pending.description: Pending: metadata is being resolved in the background, poll again

source.description:
the provider of a pasted link or id from another source than the
folder's ("anilist" for an anime in a TVDB-ordered tree); empty: the
folder's own

elsewhere.description:
Elsewhere: upcoming/missing media id -> a folder on the same server
that holds it or its direct prequel, outside this season folder. A
continuation after a break is often filed under its first season.

missing.description:
Missing: series of that season already on air for longer than the
grace period that the folder still lacks.

upcoming.description:
Upcoming: series of a season folder's season that the folder lacks
because they have not aired yet (or only just started). Anime scope,
season folders and fully matched listings only.

locale.description:
ui language at registration time, so the verify email is localized
before the first locale sync can happen

remember.description:
"stay signed in": a session that slides with use for up to 90 days
instead of one that ends with the browser and after a day at most

includeDecisions.description:
IncludeDecisions also drops the manual matches, the scope marks and the
dismissed suggestions. Off by default: nothing rebuilds those.

requeue.description:
Requeue re-runs the automatic match on every server afterwards.
Absent means true - a reset that leaves the catalog empty is not useful.

deleted.description: Deleted maps store slug to the number of rows removed.

kept.description: Kept lists the store slugs the reset deliberately left alone.

queued.description: Queued is how many folders were handed back to the matcher.

cover.description:
Cover is the item's picture and Section the list it was hidden from
(a page's own name for it, "watchlist", "upgrades"), both only for the
restore list; optional.

label.description: display title, for the restore list

season.description: season marker in the title, -1 final

full.description: name without bracket tags and paren groups

origin.description:
marked: a mark on the folder itself; shelf: the mark of the folder
above an alphabet shelf; rule: a rule on the parent; none: no source

ruleFrom.description: the parent the rule sits on

shape.description: the name shape the rule covers

error.description: *_failed: a short excerpt of the error

ip.description:
the address, an IPv6 /64, or for an account bucket the email it is
keyed by

rename.description: absent in old files, then derived

synonyms.description:
Synonyms: alternative titles of the media (AniList only), for
shortening thread titles that repeat them.

kept.description:
Kept names the entries left behind because the new folder already has
one of the same name: a move never overwrites

moved.description: Moved counts the entries now in the new folder

server.description:
Server is the configured media server, so every user's UI can name it;
empty when none is set up

url.description: the plex.tv page the user opens to authorise

auth.description:
how the server was connected: "signin" (plex.tv sign-in, the server's
own token), "token" (pasted by hand) or "env" (PLEX_TOKEN, not
changeable from the UI); empty when not configured

choose.description:
Choose: Plex and Jellyfin are both connected and none is picked yet,
so neither runs until an admin chooses

kind.description:
Kind is the media server type: "plex" | "jellyfin"; empty when not
configured

streams.description:
Streams says whether the server can store a per-episode track choice
(Plex can, Jellyfin cannot)

local.description: it lists an address on the local network

id.description: the PIN id of the sign-in

airedMapping.description:
AiredMapping: the library pairs AniList metadata with TVDB's aired
season mapping, so a watch created from this suggestion starts with it

folder.description: Plex storage folder of the show

kind.description: that library's kind: "anime" or "" (undecided), for categorising

tvdbId.description: series id for the rename profile

building.description: a background rebuild is in progress

api.probeState.description:
Probed: how the languages above were established - 0 nothing measured yet,
1 read from the container streams, 2 measuring was attempted and the
container would not answer. The card shows this so a disputed suggestion
can be judged without reading the log.

x-enum-comments.probeFailed: measuring was attempted and impossible: no ffprobe, unreadable container, host down
x-enum-comments.probeMeasured: container streams read (ffprobe, or Plex's own analysis)
x-enum-comments.probeNone: parsed out of the file names, nothing measured

airingSchedule.description:
AiringSchedule is every not-yet-aired episode AniList has dated ahead
(usually the whole current cour), for the multi-week calendar view.

color.description:
Color is the artwork's dominant colour as a hex string. The poster
frame shows it while the file loads. Empty on older cache entries
and for artwork AniList has not measured.

extraLarge.description:
ExtraLarge is the same artwork at twice the edge (460px rather than
230px). A poster tile on a phone is around 200 CSS px wide, which a
230px file has to stretch two to three times over at the device
pixel ratios those screens run at. Empty on cache entries written
before the field existed; consumers fall back to Large.

medium.description:
Medium is the 100px-wide artwork, for list rows and thumbnails
where Large would be downloaded only to be shrunk. Empty on cache
entries written before the field existed; consumers fall back to
Large.

descriptions.description:
Descriptions is the overview per UI language ("de", "en") where the
provider has more than one: TVDB and TMDB translate theirs, the
cached record serves every user, and the page picks the one its
reader speaks. Description stays the instance's default.

externalLinks.description:
ExternalLinks are the streaming and official sites AniList lists for
the title; the Crunchyroll one carries the series id the dub recorder
reads releases under (see CrunchyrollID).

nextAiringEpisode.description:
NextAiring is the upcoming episode's release slot (RELEASING titles);
nil for finished titles or cache entries predating the field.

popularity.description:
Popularity is the audience size (AniList: users on their lists, TMDB:
vote count). Comparable within one source, which is all the catalog
sorts across: the metadata source is picked per folder.

rating.description:
Rating is the net vote count AniList users gave the recommendation;
absent for TMDB, which has no votes on it.

schedule.description:
Schedule is the flattened release list (absolute episode numbers), filled
from AiringSchedule.Nodes here and from season episodes by TMDB. Ahead of
now, except for the week TMDB keeps behind it for the airings recorder.

schema.description: Schema is the payload version this entry was written with, see MediaSchema.

native.description: original-script title, stored per locale, never displayed directly

preferred.description:
Preferred is the canonical display title we compute (localized,
never native Japanese). Set by the API layer once the media's source
is known; consumers render this instead of guessing romaji/english.

type.description:
Type is ANIME or MANGA (light novels are MANGA with format NOVEL).
AniList ids are unique across both, so one id never means two works.

volumes.description:
Volumes and Chapters are the MANGA counterparts of Episodes, 0 while
the work is still running or AniList does not know.

ambiguous.description: no confident match - the user should pick

provider.description: ordering provider from Plex: tvdb | tmdb | ""

seriesId.description: resolved provider series id, 0 when none

seriesProvider.description: provider used to resolve the series id

seriesTitle.description: localized title of the resolved series

sibling.description: a marked sibling's name, for the reason

kind.description:
"" clears the mark; "none" stores "no mark", which keeps a scope rule
and the hints off this folder

rule.description:
also mark new folders beside this one whose name has the same shape
(numbers and season names vary); needs a kind and a name that varies

ruleId.description:
the rule that covers this folder (its parent and shape), 0 for none.
Scope came from it unless the folder carries a mark of its own.

ruleShape.description:
the name shape a rule made from this folder would cover; "" when its
name has nothing that varies (no number, no season) or it is the root

color.description: one of serverColors, empty = picked from the id

hostKey.description: HostKey is the pinned SSH host key's fingerprint, empty while none is trusted

icon.description: one of serverIcons, empty = the name stands alone

protocol.description: ftp: legacy rows only, no longer accepted as input

api.serverInput.description: server to create (protocol/port/password confirmed by the user)

createdAt.description: "" for sessions older than the column

aiBaseUrl.description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint (LiteLLM, OpenRouter, Ollama /v1); empty = assistant off

aiSearchUrl.description: SearXNG base for the assistant's web search; empty = off

animescheduleToken.description: write-only, dates English dub episodes ahead

arrCompleteDir.description: local folder grabs from Sonarr/Radarr land in; must be under a download root

arrKeySet.description: read-only: the Sonarr/Radarr source is on, managed via /api/settings/arr-key

arrRoots.description: newline-separated "appPath => localPath" mappings for apps that see the media under another path

baseUrl.description: public origin of this instance, used in email links

downloadRoots.description: read-only: local roots files may be written to

downloadsEnvSet.description: read-only: WEEBSYNC_DOWNLOADS is set (else only the data dir default)

envLocked.description: json field names whose value comes from an env var; the UI locks them

fieldIssues.description:
read-only: json field name -> why its stored value now fails the check a
save would run (e.g. the host no longer resolves)

forceHttps.description: always mark cookies Secure - for a proxy that terminates TLS

haWebhookUrl.description: Home Assistant webhook the backend POSTs events to; empty = off

oidcProviderName.description: login button label ("Sign in with X")

onboardingDone.description: first-run wizard finished (or an install that predates it)

plexLibRoots.description: read-only: mounts auto-detected from Plex's reported library locations (flat)

plexLibraries.description: read-only: detected mounts grouped by their Plex library

plexRoots.description: manual override: newline-separated local dirs where the Plex library is mounted; usually unneeded (auto-detected)

plexSectionAnime.description: csv of key:0|1 - does this library hold anime; missing key = guessed from title/agent

plexSectionSources.description: csv of key:source (anilist|tmdb); missing key = by library title

plexSections.description: csv of section keys, empty = all show/movie sections

plexSkipOwned.description: auto-sync leaves episodes Plex already holds (under any name) on the remote

trustedNetworks.description: csv of CIDRs/IPs that bypass the login rate limit

trustedProxies.description: csv of CIDRs/IPs whose X-Forwarded-* headers are believed

api.statusDisk.description:
Disk is the download root's filesystem, kept for consumers that read
one value; Disks is every filesystem the library spans, the root first

paths.description: Paths are the other library paths on this same filesystem

errorCode.description:
ErrorCode is the classified reason (see transfer.classifyError); empty
for a success or an unrecognized failure.

keyValid.description: the key was accepted by TMDB

focus.description:
Focus is where the banner's detail lies, for the page to pick the
slice its box shows; absent until the server has read the picture

source.description: Source is the metadata source of the title, for opening its card

tier.description:
Tier says where the title came from: one of the caller's auto-syncs,
a matched catalog folder, or the default set

title.description: Title names the panel for a screen reader; never drawn on the banner

url.description: URL is AniList's banner, full width

watches.description:
Watches is how many auto-syncs the caller has; with none the page
offers to create the first

approved.description: false while the account waits for an admin to let it in

emailVerified.description: false while a self-registered account has not confirmed its address

latest.description: latest tag (stable) or short sha of the newest build (nightly, dev)

updateCheck.description: instance setting: is the check enabled

lang.description:
Lang is the language step: what the file carries and what the watch
asked for. Absent when neither is known.

replaced.description:
Replaced is the version step: the file name of the older copy this one
moved into the trash folder (an upgrade sync, a v2 over its v1). Absent
when it replaced nothing or the trash has been emptied since.

api.watchLastLang.description:
Lang is the language step: what the file carries and what the watch
asked for. Absent when neither is known.

dub.description:
Dub and Sub are the audio and subtitle languages as app language codes
("Ger", "Jap").

from.description:
From says where they were read: name is the file's (or its folder's)
language tags, probe the tracks a header probe of the remote file found.

wantDub.description: WantDub and WantSub are the watch's language filter the file passed.

at.description: unix seconds of the next check

reason.description:
retry_backoff: the last check failed, the next one comes early
lang_backlog: files wait for their language, checks stay on the interval
until_slot: every aired episode is here, nothing happens before the slot
finished_idle: finished and complete, only the stale re-check remains
interval: the plain interval

ordering.description: raw showOrdering value, for the UI hint

provider.description:
Provider is which catalog Plex itself uses for this library ("tvdb" |
"tmdb" | ""), derived from its episode ordering. The modern Plex agent
looks the same for every library and every show carries tvdb, tmdb and
imdb guids alike, so the ordering is the only thing that tells them
apart.

attempts.description:
Attempts counts the failures behind this row so far, RetryAt (unix
seconds) says when the next attempt may start. A row waiting for its
next attempt stays queued and keeps Error/ErrorCode, so the UI can say
what went wrong and how long the wait is.

errorCode.description:
ErrorCode classifies Error into a stable machine-readable reason
(see classifyError): permission_denied, disk_full, read_only, rename_failed,
auth_failed; empty when the failure is not one we recognize.

finishedAt.description:
FinishedAt is when a finished row (done, error, canceled) ended (UTC,
as SQLite writes it), for "new here" and the history; empty while it
is still on its way. Only the list fills it.

queuePos.description: QueuePos orders the queue: the scheduler starts the lowest first.

replaceOld.description:
ReplaceOld: once this file is in place, the older copy of the same
episode next to it is moved out of the way (an upgrade sync).

info.description: Self-hosted S/FTP anime and media sync: servers, catalog, downloads, watches, suggestions and auth. The interactive docs are served only by local dev builds.
info.title: WeebSync API

delete.description: Deletes exactly one cache row (admin only). The key must belong to the scope; for the catch-all scope that means no other scope claims it.

parameters.description: full cache key (must belong to the scope)
parameters.name: key

get.description: Pages through the cache rows of one scope, optionally filtered by key substring (admin only).

Reports every rebuildable body of data in the database (caches, derived structures, recorded decisions) with row counts, size, age span, what rebuilds it and what it depends on (admin only). Names are stable slugs; the UI supplies the prose.

post.description: Empties every cache and derived data store in a single transaction and, unless requeue is false, re-runs the automatic match on every server afterwards (admin only). The remote index is kept: it is only a snapshot of the servers' directories, and dropping it would force a full re-crawl before anything could be matched at all - it stays individually deletable and is named under "kept". Recorded decisions (manual matches, scope marks, dismissed suggestions) survive unless includeDecisions is set. Takes no backup; back the database up first.

delete.description: Empties one rebuildable data store: every table it consists of, in the registry's delete order, honouring its row filter (admin only). Decision stores can be deleted here too - this endpoint asks no questions, the confirmation belongs in the UI.

get.description: The encoder the player transcodes with (NVENC, VA-API or software), the configured WEEBSYNC_HWACCEL mode and, per candidate, a machine-readable diagnosis (code + params). Before the first transcode or probe, "probed" is false and there is no choice (admin only).

post.description: Runs the test encodes again (a few seconds, at most 90) and replaces the cached choice, so new transcodes use the result. A probe already running is joined, never run twice at once (admin only).

delete.description: Drops one server's remote index (admin only); the crawler rebuilds it from the root. Catalog matches are untouched.

put.description: Sets one server's crawler interval and per-crawl budget, 0 = default (admin only).

get.description: Reports the state of all background machinery: running jobs, match queue, effective TTLs, Plex/AniList/index/watch info and per-server match stats (admin only). Cache and data store sizes live in /api/admin/data.

post.description: Stops a family of background jobs from starting, or lets them start again (admin only). A job already running is unaffected - stop it separately.

Triggers one background job by name (admin only): plex-suggestions, anilist-suggestions, index-crawl or rematch. Crawl/rematch require serverId; rematch returns a queued count, the others a started status.
Cancels the running jobs of a family (admin only). A job that checks for cancellation stops within one unit of work; one that does not stops at its next natural break.

put.description: Switches the runtime log level (admin only): trace, debug, info, warn or error. Takes effect immediately without a restart and controls what the live-log stream emits.

get.description: Streams backend log records to the admin as Server-Sent Events: the buffered recent backlog first, then live records. The volume follows the current log level.

delete.description: Removes one catalog match row, manual or automatic (admin only). The folder re-appears as pending and is rematched automatically.

get.description: Pages through one server's catalog match rows, optionally filtered and searched (admin only).

Lists what about the instance's setup weakens it, worst first, with the checks that passed (admin only). Judged partly from this very request: the transport and proxy findings describe the way the admin reached the instance.

put.description: Sets the cache TTL overrides in hours, 0..720 (0 = default), admin only.

post.description: Streams the assistant's answer as server-sent events (JSON per line: delta, tool, proposal, error, done). The model only reads; proposals are vetted server-side and confirmed by the user in the watch dialog.

get.description: Lists the model ids the configured endpoint serves plus the default. Always 200; an unreachable endpoint reports error with an empty list.
Whether an assistant endpoint is configured; force=1 also tests the connection. Always 200.

post.description: A follow-up typed while an answer streams. The running loop reads it between its rounds and the model continues with it; the stream reports it as a steer event. Not queued when no answer is streaming.

get.description: Finish the AniList OAuth flow (state check, code exchange, token storage); redirects to /settings.

delete.description: Unlink the requesting user's AniList account.

get.description: Start the AniList OAuth authorization-code flow (redirects to AniList).

delete.description: Remove a media from the linked user's list. Needs the list switch (403 otherwise). Removing a title that is not on the list is not an error.

403.description: list changes turned off in the settings

get.description: The linked user's AniList list entry for a media (status, progress, score on the 100-point scale plus the user's own score format), read with the user's token. linked=false without a connected account.

put.description: Create or change the linked user's list entry for a media: status, progress (0 to the episode count when known) and score (0-100). Only the given fields change. Needs the list switch (403 otherwise).

403.description: list changes turned off in the settings

post.description: Toggle the linked user's like on a forum thread or comment and return the new state. Needs the replies-and-likes switch (403 otherwise); rate-limited per user (429).

403.description: replies and likes turned off in the settings

get.description: Report the linked AniList account and configuration state for the settings UI.
Fetch a single AniList media entry by id.

put.description: Turn the user's AniList write switches on or off: list (status, progress, score, removal) and social (replies, likes). Both are off by default.

post.description: Set the watched-episode count of a title on the linked AniList list.

403.description: list changes turned off in the settings

get.description: Search AniList media by title, anime unless type=manga.
Watchlist titles (watching/planning) present on the user's servers, plus the AniList trending chart.

parameters.description: Set to 1 to force a watchlist refresh
parameters.name: force

get.description: Opening post and one page (25 top-level comments) of an AniList forum thread. Bodies are AniList markdown, capped in size; replies are flattened under their top-level comment, at most three levels deep. isLiked is set only for a user who allowed replies and likes.

post.description: Post a comment in a forum thread, or under one of its comments, as the linked user. Needs the replies-and-likes switch (403 otherwise); at most 10000 characters; a few per minute (429 beyond).

403.description: replies and likes turned off in the settings

post.description: Link an AniList account from a manually pasted pin-flow access token.

get.description: Report whether the configured AnimeSchedule.net token is accepted.
Reports whether OIDC is available, whether registration is open, the active auth mode and whether first-run setup is still pending. Consumed by the login page.
Reports the caller's chosen categories, which categories are available to them (admin categories only for admins) and whether SMTP delivery is configured.

put.description: Stores the caller's chosen categories, dropping any not valid for them (a non-admin cannot subscribe to admin categories).

post.description: Mails a link to set a new password, good for an hour and once. Answers the same whether or not the address has an account, so it tells nobody which addresses do; at most one mail per account every five minutes. Accounts that sign in through OIDC get none.
post.summary: Ask for a password reset link

put.description: Stores the caller's UI language (de or en) for server-delivered emails and push notifications.

post.description: Returns a session cookie on success, or a twoFactorRequired challenge (with a short-lived token) when TOTP or a security key is enrolled. Disabled while OIDC-only auth is active.
post.summary: Log in with email and password

post.description: Completes a password login by verifying the TOTP code (or a recovery code) against the short-lived pending token.
Destroys the current session and clears the session cookie.

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's id, email, admin flag, whether the account has a password, and which metadata providers have keys.

post.description: Probes a base URL (and common mount paths) for an OIDC discovery document and returns the issuer of the first hit. Open during first-run; requires an admin session afterwards.
post.summary: Probe a URL for an OIDC provider

put.description: Replaces the caller's password after checking the current one, and ends the caller's other sessions. An account that signs in through OIDC has no password to change.

get.description: Lists the per-IP auth rate-limiter state, whether each IP is currently blocked (admin only).

post.description: Unblocks one IP (by ip) or every tracked IP (all=true), admin only.
Creates an email/password account. The first account becomes admin. When SMTP is configured, later accounts must verify their email before login. Disabled while OIDC-only auth is active.
Consumes the token of a reset link (good for an hour and once), sets the new password and ends the account's sessions.
post.summary: Set a new password from a reset link

get.description: The signed-in browsers of the account, newest first.

delete.description: Signs every browser of the account out except this one.
Signs one browser of the account out. Not the current one: that is logout.

post.description: Stores an OIDC provider configuration during first-run setup, before any account exists. Only reachable while there are zero users; afterwards OIDC config requires an admin session.
While no account exists: checks the setup code (X-Setup-Token) and sets a short-lived signed cookie that lets the provider's callback create the first account. Afterwards refused.

delete.description: Turns off TOTP (and clears recovery codes) after a password re-check.

get.description: Reports whether the current user has TOTP enabled.

post.description: Verifies the first TOTP code, activates TOTP and returns 10 one-time recovery codes (shown once).
Generates a new TOTP secret (stored unconfirmed) and returns the otpauth URL and base32 secret for the authenticator app.

get.description: Consumes an email-verification token and redirects to the login page. Public: the token embedded in the link is the secret.

parameters.description: resolve the kind and fields for this folder
parameters.name: serverId

post.description: Starts a WebAuthn assertion for the enrolled security key after a correct password, keyed by the short-lived pending token.
Completes the security-key assertion and establishes a session. The ceremony id and pending token travel in the X-WA-Session and X-WA-Token headers; the body is the assertion.

get.description: Lists the current user's registered passkeys and security keys.

delete.description: Removes one of the current user's registered passkeys or security keys.

post.description: Starts a discoverable WebAuthn login ceremony and returns the ceremony id and assertion options. Disabled while OIDC-only auth is active.
Completes a discoverable WebAuthn login ceremony and establishes a session. The ceremony id travels in the X-WA-Session header; the body is the assertion.

Starts a WebAuthn registration ceremony. Send X-WA-Type: key for a cross-platform second-factor security key; otherwise a resident passkey is requested. Returns the ceremony id and credential creation options.
Completes a WebAuthn registration ceremony and stores the new credential. The ceremony id and metadata travel in headers; the request body is the credential attestation.

delete.description: Deletes a file or directory under the download root. A non-empty directory needs recursive=true. Admin only.

parameters.name: path

requestBody.description: Directory path relative to the download root

get.description: Rules that mark new folders like a marked one: same parent, same name shape (numbers and season names vary), same kind.

get.description: Series metadata for the authenticated user's downloads (same window as GET /api/downloads): one group per remote series folder with cover, description and provider links, plus one item per download with its season/episode and, when the provider cache is warm, the episode title. Kept apart from the download list because that one is polled and patched by the event stream.

requestBody.description: Queued download ids in the new order

get.description: The authenticated user's total download rate over the last ten minutes, one sample per second, so a chart opened later starts full.

Ask the configured Jellyfin server for a Quick Connect code, to read the user's favourites as their watchlist.

Related titles, recommendations, cast, external links and forum threads for a title from AniList or TMDB.
Community reviews for a title from AniList or TMDB.

The local target is probed for writability and the update is rejected when it cannot be written. With moveFiles the old target folder's entries are moved into the new one first (within one media root, never overwriting).
